newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-ENGLISH ROW THREATENS TOUR SHAMBLES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ENGLISH ROW THREATENS TOUR SHAMBLES.

text.p: Top players from Argentina, South Africa, Australia and New Zealand are set to become unwitting victims of English rugby's civil war, barring a last-minute peace deal between leading clubs and the Rugby Football Union.
Senior English officials reacted with dismay on Thursday after the clubs' confirmed they would not release players for a succession of tour matches over the next month.
The move follows the latest breakdown in talks with the RFU and threatens to wreck 13 forthcoming games involving Argentina, Queensland, South Africa A and the New Zealand Barbarians.
London will now be represented by players from third division clubs when they play the Pumas at Twickenham next Wednesday as the battle for control of the English game continues.

"It is a desperately sad day for rugby," said former national team manager Derek Morgan. "I hope some of the players' contracts have a let-out clause which allows them to play in the divisional matches.
"These games by the English provinces against strong touring opposition are specifically designed as a stepping stone into the England A team.
"We believed we had put in place a sensible pyramid towards an international cap. But one rung is being removed."
Tony Jorden, former England full-back and chairman of London selectors, has decided to withdraw his supervision of London's preparations for the encounter with the Pumas.

"Now we have to utilise players from below the first two divisions in Rosslyn Park and Havant, I can only hand over to the coaches of those two clubs and let them select and coach the side for what was supposed to be a showpiece match.

"What worries me is that players outside the top leagues will be competing against international players and that could be potentially dangerous, especially against the Argentinians who are noted as one of the most powerful scrummaging teams in the world.
